data.cultural_impact: The name Silu holds immense cultural value in Indian societies, particularly in Tamil Nadu, where it is a fairly common name. Mountains have always held a special place in Indian culture and mythology. Apart from being a symbol of power and resilience, they are also considered the source of water and other natural resources. Mountains are often the site of temples and other sacred places, making the name Silu a reminder of this rich cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Silu reflects the Hindu belief in the divine presence of the gods in mountains. It is believed that the heavenly bodies reside in mountains, and they are revered as the abode of various deities. The name Silu can inspire a sense of devotion towards these divine beings and a deep appreciation for the natural world around us. This name can also serve as a reminder of the inner strength and resilience that we all possess, much like a mountain.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Silu was a king of the Vedic Ikshvaku dynasty, mentioned in the Mahabharata. The name Silu carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Silu was a king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, who ruled over the region of Haihayas (modern day Bihar). He was a contemporary of the Pandava prince Bhima.
